chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Malik ibn Atiyya, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Ali ibn Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) said: 'I guaranteed upon my Lord that no one would ask (for something) without a need, except that the asking would compel him for a day until he would ask for a need.'
ai.seo_question: What is the consequence of asking for something without a genuine need according to Imam Ali (AS)?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam Ali ibn Al-Husayn (Zayn al-Abidin) articulates a spiritual principle where superfluous requests become a self-imposed burden, reflecting the Shia concept of *hajah* (genuine need) versus *talaqqi* (seeking). This guarantee underscores the divine wisdom that unnecessary asking disrupts contentment (*qana'ah*) and prolongs dependence, a theme deeply explored in Shia ethical literature regarding the purification of intention in supplication.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Al Hassan Bin Mahboub, from Malik Bin Atiyya,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘I<sup>asws</sup> hereby guarantee upon my<sup>asws</sup> Lord<sup>azwj</sup> that no one would beg for, without having a (real) need, except for one day, he would be desperate for it, (in a real) need’.
en.sarwar: 1. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from al-Hassan ibn Mahbub from Malik ibn ‘Atiyyah who has said the following: “Abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that

Ali ibn al-Husayn, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ’I guarantee from my Lord that whoever asks for help without actually being in need, a pressing need will force him one day (sooner or later) to ask help for an actual need.’”
